inputs.share_count_basis: Diluted weighted-average count from the H1 FY2026 interim EPS note (6,599.6m basic + 6.8m dilutive A-share ESOP shares = 6,606.3m). Shares in issue are 6,637.2m less ~41m treasury shares held for the A-share employee stock ownership schemes. Held FLAT: SBC is fully expensed in the flows, so diluting the count as well would charge it twice. No non-SBC issuance expected; the H-share IPO (258.2m shares, May 2025) is already in the count.
inputs.sbc_source: FY2025 annual report consolidated cash flow statement, 'Equity-settled share-based payment expense' RMB283,395k (FY2024: 209,255k); EquityAwardTaxes nil (A-share ESOP schemes are funded by treasury-share repurchases, not net-share settlement)
inputs.buyback_note: FY2025 repurchase of 16.6m A shares (RMB978.2m) under the A-share employee stock ownership schemes, i.e. buybacks fund the ESOP rather than retire shares; H1 FY2026 a further RMB242.8m. The flat count is therefore funded. Buybacks are value-neutral here because the ESOP cost is already charged through SBC.
inputs.fx_note: Statements and flows in RMB (CNY); H-share quote in HKD. All per-share values computed in CNY and converted at CNY/HKD 1.1731 (Yahoo CNYHKD=X, 2026-10-16). Parity check against the Shanghai A-share dual listing 600276.SH: RMB46.63 x 1.1731 = HKD54.70 vs the observed H-share HKD47.84, i.e. the H-share trades at a 12.5% A/H discount -- a normal A/H spread, which confirms the rate direction and the quote basis. The DCF values the same claim on the same flows; the A/H discount is a market-structure feature, not a valuation input. refresh_price.py does not move fx_rate: re-date it on the next rebuild.
inputs.wacc_rationale: Built in CNY, the flows' currency: 10-year China government bond ~1.8%, China equity risk premium ~6.5%, beta ~1.1 for a large-cap innovative pharma with policy-pricing exposure -> cost of equity ~9.0%; zero borrowings so WACC = cost of equity = 9.0%. Policy, pipeline and geopolitical risk are charged in the scenario flows and weights, not stacked on the discount rate, and the same WACC is used in all three scenarios.
inputs.lease_treatment: (A) leases as debt: lease liabilities RMB68.0m (29.8m current + 38.2m non-current, H1 FY2026 balance sheet) are included in total_debt and lease principal (RMB43.8m FY2025) is NOT deducted from the flows; right-of-use depreciation stays inside D&A. Immaterial either way (<0.2% of revenue).
inputs.nci_treatment: NCI deducted once, in the equity bridge at book (RMB523.3m, H1 FY2026); flows are consolidated. NCI profit share is RMB6m on RMB7.7bn, so attributable and consolidated flows are indistinguishable.
inputs.ebitda_basis: Operating adj-EBITDA (pre-SBC) is rebuilt from the P&L: gross profit less selling & distribution, R&D (expensed portion only) and administrative expenses, plus recurring government grants, less recurring donations, impairments and bill-discount charges, plus D&A and SBC. FY2025: 27,266.8 - 9,106.4 - 6,961.2 - 3,071.7 + 461.8 - 281.0 - 133.5 - 2.5 = EBIT 8,172 + D&A 942.5 + SBC 283.4 = 9,398m = 29.7% of revenue (FY2024 26.9%; H1 FY2026 31.0% vs H1 FY2025 33.6%). Excluded as non-operating, each with its matching asset in the bridge or in net cash: bank interest income 785.4m (cash), FVTPL gains 188.4m and dividends 24.8m (FVTPL assets incl. the Kailera stake), share of associates -97.1m (associates at book), net FX losses 363.4m (translation of USD deposits). The CSV's EBITDA (8,879m) is PBT + finance costs + D&A - interest and so still carries FX, FV and associate items; the component build does not. Tie-out: EBIT 8,172 x (1 - 11.4% book tax) = 7,240 NOPAT; + after-tax non-operating items (~477) = 7,717 = reported profit for the year.
inputs.capex_basis: Capex in the driver paths is PP&E purchases PLUS capitalised development expenditure (intangible purchases), because capitalised R&D is real cash the owner pays for growth: FY2025 2,961.9 + 1,841.0 = 4,802.9m = 15.2% of revenue (FY2024 13.3%; H1 FY2026 annualising ~17.8%). The CSV free_cash_flow (8,273m) deducts PP&E capex only, and FY2025 OCF also carried a ~RMB2.9bn increase in contract liabilities (licensing upfronts received ahead of recognition: 160m -> 3,077m). Both are why the component year-1 owner-FCF margin (~10%) is far below last_fcf / revenue (22.8%): neither the capitalised R&D nor the upfront prepayment is a repeatable owner cash flow at that level. Capex tapers to 8% by year 10 against D&A rising to 5.5% as the capitalised development base amortises, leaving ~2.5% of revenue of net investment for 3% terminal growth.
inputs.licensing_treatment: Licensing revenue (FY2024 2,700m, FY2025 3,392m, H1 FY2026 1,422m vs 1,991m) is lumpy and deal-timing dependent. It is NOT extrapolated from any single year. The base case normalises it at ~RMB4.5bn in FY2026 (H1 actual 1.4bn + H2 GSK/Braveheart run-rate + roughly half the BMS US$600m upfront expected in Q3 2026, with Novo's US$300m upfront and the BMS anniversary payments spread over 2027-28) and grows it ~5%/yr thereafter as a mid-cycle stream of new deals, milestones and ex-China royalties. This sits between the FY2025 actual and the contracted 2026-27 peak. Drug sales are modelled separately: innovative drugs (FY2025 16.3bn, +26%; H1 FY2026 +16.4%) at +15-16%/yr against generics (~11.7bn) shrinking ~15%/yr under VBP, which is why total drug-sales growth is only ~3-9% for the next five years (H1 FY2026 drug sales +1.9%).
inputs.notes: MODEL: owner-FCF component DCF (owner_fcf_dcf_component), routed via .claude/skills/dcf-methods/SKILL.md as an operating pharmaceutical company; adaptations applied for currency (CNY flows, HKD quote), leases, NCI, non-operating assets and the matching-asset rule. First valuation of this ticker (no prior DCF, no memory entry). Price is the HKEX regular-session print; net cash and share count are from the H1 FY2026 interim (30 June 2026). Net cash: cash and bank balances 38,721.6m less lease liabilities 68.0m = 38,653.6m; pledged deposits (12.7m) excluded. Non-operating assets whose income is stripped from the flows are added in the equity bridge (FVTPL 2,422.9m, associates 800.6m), and contract liabilities of 1,732.2m are deducted because that cash is already in net cash while the matching revenue is still in the forecast. Unrealised FX losses on USD deposits (H1 FY2026 665.5m) are excluded from operating EBITDA. Cash tax ramps from the FY2025 11.4% book / 10.7% cash rate toward the 15% High-and-New-Technology-Enterprise rate as R&D super-deductions normalise. Working capital: receivables + inventories exceed payables + contract liabilities by ~RMB4.3bn (14% of revenue), so growth consumes cash; wc_capture is negative, moderated for licensing prepayments. The H-share trades at a 12.5% discount to the A-share; the DCF makes no call on that spread.

historical_growth.growth_divergence_warning: EPS 3yr CAGR 24.6% vs revenue 14.1% and equity 17.2% (10.2% ex the RMB10.35bn H-share IPO proceeds): EPS outran revenue by >30% on margin expansion from the innovative-drug mix shift and on lumpy licensing. Neither the 14% revenue CAGR nor the 25% EPS CAGR is a forward run-rate: FY2025 revenue carried RMB3.4bn of deal-timing-dependent licensing, generics are shrinking under VBP, and H1 FY2026 revenue was -1.9%. The selected 6.8% is the base scenario's own path, not a historical extrapolation.
historical_growth.notes: Only FY2022-FY2025 annual data (four years) so 5-year CAGRs are not computable. Owner FCF (reported FCF - SBC - interest income) is available for FY2024 (4,641.0m) and FY2025 (7,204.7m) only; the +55% is distorted by the ~RMB2.9bn FY2025 contract-liability inflow from licensing upfronts and by capitalised development (1.84bn) that reported FCF omits, so no owner-FCF CAGR is used for growth selection.

base.narrative: Innovative drug sales grow 15-16%/yr on the 2026-28 approval wave while generics shrink ~15%/yr under VBP, so drug sales grow 3-9%; licensing normalised at ~RMB4.5bn growing 5%. EBITDA margin drifts from 29% to 32% on mix (86% gross margin on innovative drugs) partly offset by NRDL cuts and sustained R&D intensity; capex tapers from 15% to 8% as the capacity build and capitalised-R&D step-up mature.

bull.narrative: Pipeline conversion hits the ~53-approval target, innovative drugs compound >20% and generics decline more slowly; the BMS (up to US$15.2bn) and Novo Nordisk (up to US$2.6bn) programmes deliver milestones and the licensing stream runs at RMB6-8bn/yr with ex-China royalties layering in late decade. Margin reaches 36% as licensing and innovative mix dominate and R&D grows slower than revenue.

bear.narrative: NRDL renewals keep taking >60% price cuts, VBP round 12+ accelerates generic erosion to ~18%/yr, innovative growth slows to ~9% in crowded PD-1/ADC/CDK4/6 categories, and BIOSECURE-style scrutiny plus a biotech funding downturn cut licensing to ~RMB2.5bn/yr. R&D stays at ~27% of revenue to defend the pipeline, so margin compresses to 25%.

scenario_narratives.base: Hengrui becomes a predominantly innovative-drug company by 2028: innovative sales (FY2025 RMB16.3bn, 58% of drug sales) grow 15-16%/yr on the ~53 approvals management targets for 2026-28, while the RMB11.7bn generic book shrinks ~15%/yr under successive VBP rounds, so total drug sales grow only 3-9%/yr. Licensing is treated as a normalised mid-cycle stream (~RMB4.5bn, +5%/yr) rather than a run-rate of the BMS/Novo upfronts. The operating EBITDA margin drifts from 29% to 32% as the 86%-gross-margin innovative mix rises, partly offset by NRDL cuts and R&D held near 22% of revenue. Capex (incl. capitalised R&D) tapers from 15% of revenue to 8% as the manufacturing build and the capitalised-development step-up mature; cash tax ramps from ~12% to the 15% HNTE rate. Owner-FCF margin matures from ~10% to ~19% by year 10.
scenario_narratives.bull: The bull axes are pipeline conversion and deal flow. Approvals arrive on schedule, GLP-1/metabolic (ribupatide, HRS9531, HRS-1596) and ADC franchises scale, innovative drugs compound >20% for five years, generics decline more slowly, and the BMS/Novo/Kailera relationships convert into milestones and royalties so licensing runs at RMB6-8bn/yr. Revenue grows 11-13% through 2030; EBITDA margin reaches 36%; capex falls to 7% of revenue. This needs pipeline, deal flow and margins to all deliver, which is why its weight is held at 25%.
scenario_narratives.bear: The bear axes are domestic pricing policy and cross-border politics. NRDL negotiations keep extracting >60% cuts on newly listed innovative drugs, VBP keeps compressing generics at ~18%/yr, PD-1/ADC/CDK4/6 competition from BeiGene/BeOne, Innovent, Junshi and Hansoh caps innovative growth near 9%, and BIOSECURE-type scrutiny plus a multinational capital-allocation downturn cut licensing to ~RMB2.5bn/yr. Revenue is flat in FY2026 and grows 1-4.5% thereafter; margin compresses to 25% as R&D is defended at ~27% of revenue. The balance sheet (RMB38.7bn net cash, no borrowings) means there is no solvency path: the bear case is a slow-growth, lower-margin pharma, not a distressed one.

probability_weighted.weights_rationale: Moved from the 15/50/35 house default to 25/50/25. Bear raised to 25% because pricing is set by a single regulator (NRDL/VBP) whose 2025 round averaged >60% cuts, and because an increasing share of value depends on cross-border licensing exposed to US-China biotech politics. Bull lowered to 25% because it requires three independent things to go right at once: on-schedule pipeline conversion, sustained multinational deal flow, and margin expansion against NRDL cuts. Base at 50%: the debt-free balance sheet, the 25,000-hospital channel and the demonstrated licensing track record (seven major deals in 2025-26) make the middle path the modal outcome.

valuation_philosophy.summary: Value Hengrui as the owner cash flow of its China drug franchise plus a normalised, mid-cycle out-licensing stream, with capitalised R&D charged as capex and interest, fair-value and FX items stripped and matched by their assets in the bridge. The net cash pile (RMB38.7bn, ~RMB5.85/share) is added at book. The resulting value is what a 9% CNY discount rate pays for 5-8% near-term growth maturing to a ~19% owner-FCF margin; the market's ~40x P/E on the A-share implies either the bull pipeline/deal path or a much lower required return, and the required-return table shows which.
key_risks_to_valuation: NRDL renewal price cuts (>60% in the 2025 round) and VBP rounds on the generic book: the single largest driver of the bear-base spread
Licensing revenue is deal-timing dependent; the base normalises it at ~RMB4.5bn and a multi-year gap in deal flow would push the stream toward the bear's RMB2.5bn
Pipeline/clinical execution against the ~53-approval 2026-28 target; a cluster of failures removes the innovative-growth engine the base case relies on
US-China biotech policy (BIOSECURE-type legislation, DoD listings of Chinese CROs) complicating future multinational deals or HSR clearances
Capitalised R&D treated as capex (15% of revenue today) is a judgment: treating it as pure growth investment would raise value materially, treating it as perpetual would lower it
RMB/USD volatility on USD deposits and USD deal proceeds (H1 FY2026 unrealised FX loss RMB665.5m), excluded from operating flows but a real swing in reported profit
FX bridge CNY->HKD 1.1731 dated 2026-10-16 is not refreshed by price-only updates; the 12.5% A/H discount is a market-structure spread the model does not take a view on
